content: 1. Magnesium hydroxide reduces the effects of sodium phosphates (IV) by binding cations in the gastrointestinal tract. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 2. Magnesium hydroxide decreases serum phosphate levels by binding dietary phosphate. Alternative treatments should be considered if available. 3. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride increase the toxicity of aluminum hydroxide through mechanisms involving fluid and electrolyte abnormalities. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. Co-administration may increase the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. 4. Sodium sulfate, potassium sulfate, and magnesium sulfate increase the toxicity of aluminum hydroxide through similar mechanisms. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 5. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by increasing gastric pH, which decreases velpatasvir solubility (practically insoluble at pH > 5). This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored, and administration should be separated by at least 4 hours. 6. Aluminum hydroxide decreases sotalol levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended, with administration separated by 2 hours. 7. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the effects of sparsentan by increasing gastric pH, which may decrease sparsentan exposure and reduce its efficacy. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored, and sparsentan should be administered 2 hours before or after antacids. 8.
